title: A struct with methods
description:
Write a `Rectangle` struct with methods:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
struct Rectangle { x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64 }   // (x, y) is the top-left corner

impl Rectangle {
    fn new(x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64) -> Option<Rectangle>   // None for a width or height <= 0
    fn square(x: f64, y: f64, side: f64) -> Option<Rectangle>
    fn area(&self) -> f64
    fn perimeter(&self) -> f64
    fn is_square(&self) -> bool
    fn contains_point(&self, px: f64, py: f64) -> bool        // edges count as inside
    fn overlaps(&self, other: &Rectangle) -> bool            // touching edges do not count
    fn scale(&mut self, factor: f64)                         // keeps the corner, scales the size
    fn into_square(self) -> Rectangle                        // a square with the same corner and the smaller side
}
```

y grows downwards, as on a screen: the bottom edge is at `y + height`.

starter.solution.rs:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
struct Rectangle {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
    width: f64,
    height: f64,
}

hints: Methods that only measure take `&self`; `scale` changes the rectangle so it takes `&mut self`; `into_square` consumes it with `self` (still usable afterwards here, because the struct is `Copy`).
Two rectangles overlap when each one starts before the other ends, on both axes.
